solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: material that has been treated has been processed and changed, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician has been caring for a Kurdish patient who drinks heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' looks like the doctor's medical work, but it tells you to rearrange KURD AN, which then follows DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone habitually intoxicated by liquor is an alcoholic; the noun sense here is a direct synonym.

blocks.note: something popular or fashionable is 'in'
an exploit is a bold act or feat

explanation.surface: A well-liked act of daring is certainly a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb, but here it is the noun meaning a heroic feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as emphatic adverbs of agreement, confirming a statement is certainly true.

clue.text: Ginger Spice in queue for underwear

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls is Geri Halliwell
a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A pop star stands waiting in a shop queue to buy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger Spice was the stage name of Geri Halliwell in the 1990s girl group the Spice Girls; her first name sits inside LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is the general term for women's underclothes and nightwear, so underwear is a broader synonym.

indicators.note: in a down entry, something placed under another comes after it, so the second piece named goes on top

blocks.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Is there nothing at all to shelter beneath at the seaside?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the O sits beneath LID.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public bathing place or beach resort, the name taken from the Venice Lido sandbar.

blocks.note: surface reading: a worker who is not ready to stop working young
setter's reading: retiring means going to bed, so this is someone who never goes to bed early

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like leaving a career, but to retire is also to go to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who habitually stays up late into the small hours is never in bed early.

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer edge, so only its two end letters are kept

blocks.note: eras are times or periods of history
the first and last letters of the word editor

explanation.surface: The editor of The Times newspaper works out of a rubber-walled office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means periods. In British English a rubber is what Americans call an eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is the British word for the small block used to rub out pencil marks.

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in sequence

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of the word

explanation.surface: A thought occurred to someone that the middleman had been strangely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'strangely', but it means the odd letters, which are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or concept formed in the mind, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Be one about to lead nation

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
to lead an organisation is to run it

explanation.surface: An encouragement to step up and be the person who governs the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the noun, but it is the verb 'run', which goes inside BE plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich sultanate on the island of Borneo, an example of a country.

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
gear is an informal word for clothes
the boss of a newspaper is the editor, ED for short

explanation.surface: The editor's party outfit came out crumpled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a verb with 'Party' as its subject, but both are nouns giving separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded-down corners, worn from use, look like a dog's floppy ears, hence crumpled.

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters are a run taken from within

blocks.note: the four letters run consecutively across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Does a royal lady necessarily need a man in her life?
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne is the British monarch's sister, holder of the title Princess Royal. 'Wanting' looks like desire but only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, is the best-known British royal of that title and given name.

clue.text: Nailed body part to table finally?

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a limb fixed to a table with nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nailed' sounds like hammering, but it means having a nail, as a digit of the foot does.
explanation.definitionFit: Each digit of the foot carries a toenail, so a toe is literally a body part bearing a nail.

clue.text: Sea dog in battered coastal location

indicators.note: something battered has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old sailor turns up worse for wear in some seaside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea dog' looks like the sailor, but its letters plus IN are the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a Californian city on the Pacific shore, an example of a place by the sea.

clue.text: Move abroad good coming into Arab state

indicators.note: something coming into a place enters it, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
an emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf

explanation.surface: Settling overseas in a Gulf state is a good move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' looks like praise for the move, but it is just the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle in another, which is relocating overseas.

blocks.note: first meaning: a comedian with the surname Wax, named by example
second meaning: a precious stone of deep red colour

explanation.surface: Sealing wax being used in place of a red jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby Wax is an American-born comedian and TV presenter well known in Britain; 'for one' says she is an example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's first name doubles as the precious stone, a variety of corundum coloured crimson.

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement departs from the normal one, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician spots an odd rest marking lasting three bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-bar rest' reads as a musical pause; the hyphenated word is the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a breather means pausing briefly to recover, an informal word for a short break.

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so only the outer letters survive
says the same emptying treatment is applied a second time

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A nervous football fan sees both England and Germany bitterly disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for devastated, which suits the football picture, but here it means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge, tense and nervous is the informal sense of this adjective.

blocks.note: first meaning: cowardly, as in 'too chicken to try'
second meaning: the bright colour of the songbird's feathers

explanation.walkthrough: The two birds suggest choosing between pets, but each word is an adjective: one for cowardice, one a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lacking courage, and canary is a bright shade of that colour.

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as 'this writer', which is 'I'
with 'I' as subject, 'maligns' becomes 'slander', speaking falsely against someone

explanation.surface: The author admits to badmouthing someone from Samoa.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb has to agree with I, so 'maligns' turns into the first-person form.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a Pacific island nation, so its people are an example of those living on islands.

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tasty drink made by someone from Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cretan' looks like a person from Crete, fitting Greek myth, but it is only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the drink of the gods; it now means any sweet, delightful drink.

clue.text: With which each grebe generally starts?

definitions.text: With which each grebe generally starts?

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A naturalist's question about how a water bird begins life.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the instruction: every grebe hatches from one, and the initials spell it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds such as grebes begin life inside a shell laid by the mother, so this is where each starts.

clue.text: One’s business is picking up or dropping off?

definitions.text: One’s business is picking up or dropping off?

blocks.note: surface reading: catching an illness or nodding off to sleep
setter's reading: a vehicle whose trade is collecting and delivering passengers

explanation.walkthrough: The phrases suggest catching a cold or falling asleep, but read literally they describe collecting and setting down fares.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire earns its living by collecting passengers and setting them down at their destinations.

clue.text: Archer William to have noticeable effect

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple off his son's head
second meaning: as when strain begins to show its impact

explanation.surface: The legendary bowman is going to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss legend; the verb is used as in 'the pressure began to tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: When stress or fatigue starts to tell, it shows a visible impact, an idiomatic verb sense.

blocks.note: surface reading: a show in London's theatre district
setter's reading: a musical about animals that mew

explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatreland. 'Mewsical' blends musical with mew, the sound a feline makes, pointing at the long-running Lloyd Webber show.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running stage show about felines, based on T. S. Eliot poems, ran for decades in London.

clue.text: Everyone prepared to follow British sport

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the earlier-named pieces are placed second

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
everyone is all of them
someone game is willing or ready to do something

explanation.surface: Everybody is ready to back a British team at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' as an adjective means up for it, ready to have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Football, cricket or tennis are games played with a ball, examples of a kind of sport.

blocks.note: to go is to depart
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Advice to make money by heading northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise dough' sounds like fundraising, since dough is slang for money, but it is baking.
explanation.definitionFit: To make bread rise by adding yeast or another agent is the verb sense, a baking term.

indicators.note: something working is in operation and being processed, so the letters are put through a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for money while holding down a job at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: A big wheel is the British name for a Ferris wheel; 'working' looks like a job but signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant revolving passenger wheel is one of the classic rides at travelling funfairs.
